claims.label: Shining · Neo Revelation
claims.paper: Cosmos Holofoil, in the illustration window
claims.note: Bulbapedia names Shining Gyarados and Shining Magikarp as Cosmos holofoils, and a standard Cosmos holo rare foils the illustration window. These are the English printings: the Japanese versions carried a full-card foil pattern, which is a different physical card and belongs to the language axis, not to this row.

claims.label: Shining · Neo Destiny
claims.paper: A metallic sheen over the Pokémon itself — the sheet is unnamed
claims.note: Bulbapedia: the artwork carries "a reflective foil treatment on the Pokémon itself". Flipside Gaming describes the set replacing Neo Revelation's full-card pattern with "a unique metallic sheen covering the Pokémon itself". The area is documented and the paper is not, so no sheet is borrowed — and the 2002 Cosmos era rule must not answer here, because the foil is the Pokémon rather than the window.

claims.label: Shining · Shining Legends
claims.paper: The Neo Destiny sheen repeated, described as special textured foil
claims.note: Flipside Gaming: the Neo Destiny look "was replicated in the Shining Legends expansion". Bulbapedia: their holographic pattern "is similar to the ones released in Neo Destiny". A card-list site calls the finish "special textured foil", which is appearance rather than a named sheet, so the paper stays unnamed and no texture is borrowed.

claims.label: Shining · Celebrations reprint
claims.paper: Special textured foil treatment; the area is not restated
claims.note: Bulbapedia: Shining Magikarp "was re-released with a Pokémon 25th Anniversary stamp and special textured foil treatment in the Celebrations special expansion as a Classic Collection retro card." The finish is named, the area is not, so this row claims no mask rather than inheriting Neo Destiny's.

claims.label: Shining · 30th Celebration reprint
claims.paper: Textured confetti Holofoil — the Classic Collection paper
claims.note: Bulbapedia on this printing: "The 30th Celebration reprint features a gold border, a glittery Holofoil finish, and the Pokémon 30th Anniversary logo", and on the subset: "Classic Collection cards have a textured confetti holofoil pattern", with a golden border in the Mega Evolution Series. That is the registry row this build files as Pixel / Confetti, so the paper is named rather than inherited from Neo Destiny or Celebrations. No source states which cells of the face carry it, so no area is claimed, and the HD Cosmos the database used to guess for this set is gone.

claims.label: Shining · SM Black Star Promos
claims.paper: "Foil promo card" — neither paper nor area is named
claims.note: Shining Ho-Oh (SM70), Shining Celebi (SM79) and Shining Lugia (SM82) shipped in the Shining Legends Super-Premium Collection: "a never-before-seen foil promo card featuring Shining Ho-Oh" and "2 never-before-seen foil promo cards featuring Shining Lugia and Shining Celebi". "Foil" is the whole of the product copy's claim, so the paper and its area stay unnamed.

claims.label: Pokémon ★ · EX era
claims.paper: Gold-tinted holo — "golden tinges and holographic shadows" on various parts
claims.note: Bulbapedia on Pokémon ★: "Golden tinges and holographic shadows are added to various parts of the card", under the rarity rare Holo ☆. "Various parts" is not a rectangle, so no mask is claimed — the illustration window must not be assumed. `special-treatment` is the registry row for an identified paper with no sheet; it ships no texture, so these cards render plain foil instead of borrowing an era paper.

claims.label: Radiant Pokémon · Astral Radiance onward
claims.paper: Etched, embossed silver foil over the whole card, with a textured figure
claims.note: Bulbapedia: Radiant Pokémon "have a special holofoil layer" and the rarity Radiant rare, introduced in Astral Radiance. A collector guide describes the finish as "etched, embossed silver foil covering the entire card"; a second account puts textured foil on the Pokémon figure with a geometric pattern running through the card body. The area is the whole face on two sources. The paper is now painted: `radiant-etched` samples a procedural etched lattice written to `public/foil/radiant-etched/sheet.png`, and `textureVerified` is false there, so the identification and the reproduction stay separate claims. NOT Radiant Collection: that is the 2013 Legendary Treasures / Generations RC subset with one motif per card (`radiant`), and the two must never share a lookup.

claims.label: Shiny Vault · Hidden Fates
claims.paper: A special embossed Holofoil treatment — the repeat is unnamed
claims.note: Shiny Vault is the Shiny Pokémon subset: 45 Rare Shiny cards and 35 shiny printings of GX Pokémon under Rare Shiny GX, and Bulbapedia says of the subset that "All have a special embossed Holofoil treatment." The finish is documented; the repeat is not, and no source states the foil area, so this row claims no pattern and no mask. Two collector guides call the look "Galaxy holo", but that label is documented as another name for Cosmos — the 2000-2011 sheet — so adopting it would put a 2011 paper on a 2019 card. The search for a named paper is recorded: Bulbapedia opens its Cosmos page "often referred to as Galaxy Holofoil", and folio.fyi's pattern guide answers that galaxy is "another name for Cosmos" while filing "textured or etched" as relief "not a fourteenth pattern". So the one name offered for this finish is the Cosmos nickname, and the finish is a treatment rather than a sheet; borrowing Cosmos would put a 2011 paper on a 2019 card. What the finish does earn is relief: `surface-textures.ts` routes these rarities to their own granular `sparkle` normal map, so the card renders embossed while no sheet is borrowed.

claims.label: Shiny Vault · Paldean Fates
claims.paper: A holographic silver textured foil border, with textured artwork
claims.note: Bulbapedia: "Paldean Fates introduces a second rendition of Shiny Rare ... It uses a single hollow gold star", and Shiny Ultra Rare marks shiny printings of normally Ultra Rare cards. The finish is documented outside Bulbapedia: Bleeding Cool reports that the "Baby Shiny" cards carry a "holographic, silver, textured foil border" which Japan did not get, and PokéBeach confirms that "The shiny Pokemon in our set have holo borders ...
